original_english: The Earth is home to an enormous variety of life forms, and this immense variety of living organisms is known as biodiversity.
hinglish_roman: Prithvi par bahut saari life forms payi jaati hain, aur is vishal variety of living organisms ko biodiversity kehte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Biodiversity is essential for us and every organism plays a role in keeping nature stable and functioning.
hinglish_roman: Biodiversity hamare liye essential hai aur har organism nature ko stable aur functional rakhne mein ek role play karta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Microscopic algae in the oceans release most of the oxygen we breathe.
hinglish_roman: Oceans mein microscopic algae zyaadatar oxygen release karti hain jo hum saans lete hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fungi and bacteria decompose fallen leaves and convert waste into manure, making the soil fertile.
hinglish_roman: Fungi aur bacteria gire hue patte decompose karte hain aur waste ko manure mein convert karte hain, jisse mitti fertile banti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Birds, bees and bats pollinate flowers, while plants capture sunlight to prepare food that supports nearly all life on the planet.
hinglish_roman: Pakshi, bees aur bats phoolon ko pollinate karte hain, jabki plants sunlight capture karke almost sabhi jeevon ka food prepare karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: India's natural landscape is diverse, with mountains in the north, deserts in the west, and rainforests in the North East.
hinglish_roman: India ka natural landscape bahut diverse hai - uttar mein mountains, paschim mein desert, aur North East mein rainforests hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Species restricted to particular regions of the world and not found naturally anywhere else are called endemic species.
hinglish_roman: Jo species sirf kisi ek particular region mein payi jaati hain aur kahin aur naturally nahi milti, unhe endemic species kehte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Nilgiri tahr, Lion-tailed macaque, Nepenthes khasiana and Neelakurinji are endemic species found only in India.
hinglish_roman: Nilgiri tahr, Lion-tailed macaque, Nepenthes khasiana aur Neelakurinji sirf India mein payi jaane waali endemic species hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Regions that support a large number of endemic species and have undergone significant habitat loss are known as biodiversity hotspots.
hinglish_roman: Jo regions bahut saari endemic species ko support karte hain aur jahaan significant habitat loss hua ho, unhe biodiversity hotspots kehte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The Western Ghats, Indo-Burma including North East India, the Himalayas, and Sundaland are some examples of global biodiversity hotspots.
hinglish_roman: Western Ghats, Indo-Burma jisme North East India bhi shaamil hai, Himalayas aur Sundaland kuch global biodiversity hotspots ke examples hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Small differences among individuals affected their chances of survival and reproduction, helping them adapt to changed conditions.
hinglish_roman: Individuals mein choti choti differences unke survival aur reproduction ke chances ko affect karti thi, jinse woh changed conditions mein adapt kar sake.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Scientists group and classify organisms based on their shared characteristics and evolutionary relationships.
hinglish_roman: Scientists organisms ko unke shared characteristics aur evolutionary relationships ke aadhar par group aur classify karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: External features like shape, size and body organisation are used as one of the criteria to classify living organisms.
hinglish_roman: Shape, size aur body organisation jaise external features living organisms ko classify karne ke ek criterion ke roop mein use kiye jaate hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Mode of nutrition, whether autotrophic or heterotrophic, is another important criterion for classifying organisms.
hinglish_roman: Nutrition ka mode, yaani autotrophic hai ya heterotrophic, organisms ko classify karne ka ek aur important criterion hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Cell structure, whether the organism is unicellular or multicellular, eukaryote or prokaryote, is a key classification criterion.
hinglish_roman: Cell structure - organism unicellular hai ya multicellular, eukaryote hai ya prokaryote - classification ka ek key criterion hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Genetic similarity, studied through DNA analysis, helps scientists understand shared ancestry among organisms.
hinglish_roman: Genetic similarity, jo DNA analysis se study ki jaati hai, scientists ko organisms ke beech shared ancestry samajhne mein help karti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Similar features in organisms suggest that they have evolved from common ancestors.
hinglish_roman: Organisms mein similar features yeh suggest karte hain ki woh common ancestors se evolved hue hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Just like organising a library makes finding books easier, classifying organisms helps us study millions of life forms systematically.
hinglish_roman: Jaise library mein books ko organize karne se unhe dhoondna aasaan hota hai, waisi hi organisms ko classify karne se laakhon life forms ka systematic study ho sakta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Biological classification is a scientific system of grouping living organisms based on their similarities and differences.
hinglish_roman: Biological classification ek scientific system hai jisme living organisms ko unki similarities aur differences ke aadhar par group kiya jaata hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Classification supports biodiversity conservation by identifying organisms that are under the threat of extinction.
hinglish_roman: Classification un organisms ki pehchaan karke biodiversity conservation mein madad karta hai jo extinction ke khatre mein hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Aristotle grouped animals based on their habitat — land, water and air — in the 4th century BCE.
hinglish_roman: Aristotle ne 4th century BCE mein animals ko unke habitat ke aadhar par — zameen, paani aur hawa — group kiya tha.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: In the two kingdom system introduced in the 18th century, all living organisms were divided into Plantae and Animalia.
hinglish_roman: 18th century mein introduce kiya gaya two kingdom system mein sabhi living organisms ko Plantae aur Animalia mein divide kiya gaya tha.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The two kingdom system created confusion because organisms like Amoeba and Paramecium are unicellular and could not be clearly placed in Plantae or Animalia.
hinglish_roman: Two kingdom system mein confusion tha kyunki Amoeba aur Paramecium jaise organisms unicellular hain aur inhe clearly Plantae ya Animalia mein nahi rakha ja sakta tha.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Ernst Haeckel added a third kingdom Protista in 1866 to include unicellular microscopic organisms.
hinglish_roman: Ernst Haeckel ne 1866 mein unicellular microscopic organisms ko include karne ke liye teesra kingdom Protista add kiya.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Since bacteria lack a membrane-bound nucleus unlike Amoeba, they were placed in a separate kingdom called Monera, leading to a four kingdom system.
hinglish_roman: Kyunki bacteria mein Amoeba ke unlike membrane-bound nucleus nahi hota, isliye bacteria ko alag kingdom Monera mein rakha gaya, jisse four kingdom system bana.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Robert H. Whittaker proposed the five kingdom classification in 1969, which includes Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.
hinglish_roman: Robert H. Whittaker ne 1969 mein five kingdom classification propose kiya, jisme Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae aur Animalia shamil hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: In the five kingdom classification, organisms are grouped based on cell type, cell structure, level of organisation and mode of nutrition.
hinglish_roman: Five kingdom classification mein organisms ko cell type, cell structure, level of organisation aur mode of nutrition ke basis par group kiya jaata hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Kingdom Monera includes unicellular prokaryotes such as bacteria, archaea and cyanobacteria.
hinglish_roman: Kingdom Monera mein unicellular prokaryotes aate hain jaise bacteria, archaea aur cyanobacteria.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Bacteria are found everywhere, including soil, water, air, hot springs and even inside the human body.
hinglish_roman: Bacteria har jagah paaye jaate hain — mitti, paani, hawa, hot springs aur yahan tak ki human body ke andar bhi.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Cyanobacteria were among the first organisms to produce oxygen through photosynthesis, about 2.5 billion years ago.
hinglish_roman: Cyanobacteria un pehle organisms mein se the jo approximately 2.5 billion saal pehle photosynthesis ke zariye oxygen produce karte the.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Kingdom Protista includes all single-celled eukaryotes such as Amoeba, Paramecium and Euglena.
hinglish_roman: Kingdom Protista mein sabhi single-celled eukaryotes aate hain jaise Amoeba, Paramecium aur Euglena.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Protists are an important link in aquatic food chains — some produce oxygen while others serve as food for small animals.
hinglish_roman: Protists aquatic food chains mein ek important link hain — kuch oxygen produce karte hain jabki doosre chote animals ke liye food ka kaam karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Kingdom Fungi are mostly multicellular eukaryotes with cell walls made of chitin.
hinglish_roman: Kingdom Fungi mein zyaadatar multicellular eukaryotes hote hain jinki cell wall chitin se bani hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fungi are important decomposers that feed on dead organic matter such as fallen leaves, twigs or dead organisms.
hinglish_roman: Fungi important decomposers hote hain jo dead organic matter jaise gire patte, twigsaur marey hue organisms par feed karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Yeast is a unicellular fungus and since its cell wall is made of chitin, it is placed under Kingdom Fungi.
hinglish_roman: Yeast ek unicellular fungus hai aur kyunki iski cell wall chitin se bani hai, ise Kingdom Fungi mein rakha gaya hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fungi like Aspergillus and Penicillium are used to make enzymes and antibiotics.
hinglish_roman: Aspergillus aur Penicillium jaise fungi enzymes aur antibiotics banane ke kaam aate hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Kingdom Plantae includes multicellular autotrophic organisms whose cells have a rigid cell wall primarily made of cellulose.
hinglish_roman: Kingdom Plantae mein multicellular autotrophic organisms aate hain jinke cells mein ek rigid cell wall hoti hai jo mainly cellulose se bani hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Thallophytes are among the simplest plant forms, mostly found in water or moist environments, and form a simple undifferentiated body called a thallus.
hinglish_roman: Thallophytes sabse simple plant forms mein se hain, jo zyaadatar paani ya nami waale environments mein paaye jaate hain aur ek simple undifferentiated body banate hain jise thallus kehte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Bryophytes like mosses and liverworts represent an important shift from water to land but still require moisture for survival.
hinglish_roman: Bryophytes jaise mosses aur liverworts paani se zameen par aane ka ek important shift represent karte hain lekin inhe abhi bhi nami ki zaroorat hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom because they require water for reproduction.
hinglish_roman: Bryophytes ko plant kingdom ke amphibians kaha jaata hai kyunki inhe reproduction ke liye paani ki zaroorat padti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Pteridophytes like ferns possess true roots, stems and leaves, along with vascular tissues — xylem and phloem — for transporting water and food.
hinglish_roman: Ferns jaise pteridophytes mein true roots, stems aur leaves hote hain, saath hi xylem aur phloem jaise vascular tissues bhi hote hain jo paani aur food transport karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Pteridophytes still depend on water for reproduction and do not produce seeds.
hinglish_roman: Pteridophytes abhi bhi reproduction ke liye paani par depend karte hain aur seeds produce nahi karte.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Gymnosperms like pines and cycads are well adapted to cold and dry regions; their needle-like leaves reduce water loss.
hinglish_roman: Pines aur cycads jaise gymnosperms thande aur sukhe regions ke liye achhi tarah se adapt hain; unke needle-like patte paani ka nuksan kam karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Gymnosperms do not require water for fertilisation; their seeds are not enclosed in fruits but are exposed on cones.
hinglish_roman: Gymnosperms ko fertilisation ke liye paani ki zaroorat nahi hoti; unke seeds fruits mein band nahi hote balki cones par khule hote hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Angiosperms or flowering plants represent the most complex plant body organisation and are the most diverse plant group on Earth.
hinglish_roman: Angiosperms yaani flowering plants sabse complex plant body organisation represent karte hain aur yeh Earth par sabse zyaada diverse plant group hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Angiosperms produce flowers and fruits — flowers attract pollinators and fruits help disperse seeds to new locations.
hinglish_roman: Angiosperms phool aur fruits produce karte hain — phool pollinators ko attract karte hain aur fruits seeds ko nayi jagahon tak pahunchane mein madad karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Kingdom Animalia includes multicellular heterotrophic organisms that depend on other organisms for food.
hinglish_roman: Kingdom Animalia mein multicellular heterotrophic organisms aate hain jo apne food ke liye doosre organisms par depend karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Animals are classified into non-chordata and chordata based on the presence or absence of a notochord.
hinglish_roman: Animals ko notochord ki presence ya absence ke aadhar par non-chordata aur chordata mein classify kiya jaata hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Porifera or sponges are multicellular animals that lack true tissues and organs, with numerous pores allowing water to flow through their bodies.
hinglish_roman: Porifera yaani sponges multicellular animals hain jinmein true tissues aur organs nahi hote, aur unke body mein bahut saare pores hote hain jisse paani andar-bahar bahta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Cnidarians like Hydra, jellyfish and corals have tissue-level organisation and use tentacles for capturing prey.
hinglish_roman: Hydra, jellyfish aur corals jaise cnidarians mein tissue-level organisation hota hai aur yeh shikaar pakadne ke liye tentacles use karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Platyhelminthes or flatworms show bilateral symmetry, which allows better coordination of movement and directional activity.
hinglish_roman: Platyhelminthes yaani flatworms mein bilateral symmetry hoti hai, jisse movement ka better coordination aur directional activity possible hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Nematoda or roundworms have an elongated cylindrical body with two openings — a mouth and an anus.
hinglish_roman: Nematoda yaani roundworms ka body elongated aur cylindrical hota hai jisme do openings hote hain — ek mouth aur ek anus.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Annelids like earthworms have segmented bodies, which allows greater flexibility and more precise control of movement.
hinglish_roman: Earthworms jaise annelids ka body segmented hota hai, jisse movement mein zyaada flexibility aur precise control milta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Arthropods have a hard external skeleton called an exoskeleton that provides protection and reduces water loss.
hinglish_roman: Arthropods mein ek hard external skeleton hota hai jise exoskeleton kehte hain, jo protection deta hai aur paani ka loss kam karta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Mollusca like snails, squids and octopuses have soft bodies, with many having a shell for protection.
hinglish_roman: Snails, squids aur octopuses jaise mollusca ka body soft hota hai aur bahut se molluscs ke paas protection ke liye ek shell hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Echinoderms like starfish and sea urchins possess a hard internal skeleton made of calcium carbonate.
hinglish_roman: Starfish aur sea urchins jaise echinoderms mein calcium carbonate se bana ek hard internal skeleton hota hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Protochordates like Amphioxus possess a notochord at least once during their life and help us understand how chordates evolved from simpler forms.
hinglish_roman: Amphioxus jaise protochordates mein apni zindagi mein kam se kam ek baar notochord zaroor hoti hai, aur yeh samajhne mein help karte hain ki chordates kaise simpler forms se evolve hue.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Vertebrates possess a vertebral column or backbone that supports the body and protects vital organs like the brain and spinal cord.
hinglish_roman: Vertebrates mein ek vertebral column yaani backbone hota hai jo body ko support karta hai aur brain aur spinal cord jaise vital organs ki raksha karta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Vertebrates are classified into five groups — fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals — based on habitat, body covering and reproduction.
hinglish_roman: Vertebrates ko paanch groups mein classify kiya jaata hai — fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds aur mammals — habitat, body covering aur reproduction ke basis par.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fish have fins and gills that allow them to move and breathe in water.
hinglish_roman: Fish ke paas fins aur gills hote hain jo unhe paani mein chalne aur saans lene mein help karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Birds have feathers and hollow bones, which make flight possible.
hinglish_roman: Pakshiyon ke paas feathers aur hollow bones hote hain jo udon ko possible banate hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Mammals have mammary glands that produce milk for their young, improving the survival of offspring.
hinglish_roman: Mammals mein mammary glands hote hain jo apne bachhon ke liye milk produce karte hain, jisse unke survival chances badh jaate hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Classification follows a hierarchical arrangement from Kingdom at the broadest level down to Species at the most specific level.
hinglish_roman: Classification ek hierarchical arrangement follow karta hai — sabse broad level Kingdom se lekar sabse specific level Species tak.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The levels of classification in order from broadest to most specific are: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus and Species.
hinglish_roman: Classification ke levels broad se specific order mein hain: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus aur Species.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: At each lower level of the hierarchy, organisms share more common features with each other.
hinglish_roman: Hierarchy ke har neeche waale level par organisms ke beech zyaada common features hote hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The tiger belongs to Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Carnivora, Family Felidae, Genus Panthera and Species P. tigris.
hinglish_roman: Tiger Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Carnivora, Family Felidae, Genus Panthera aur Species P. tigris se belong karta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Binomial nomenclature is a universal system of naming living organisms, where every organism is given a two-part scientific name.
hinglish_roman: Binomial nomenclature living organisms ko naam dene ka ek universal system hai jisme har organism ko ek do-hissa scientific naam diya jaata hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Binomial nomenclature was introduced by Carolus Linnaeus in the 18th century.
hinglish_roman: Binomial nomenclature ko 18th century mein Carolus Linnaeus ne introduce kiya tha.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: In the binomial system, the scientific name has two parts — the genus name comes first with a capital letter, followed by the species name in lowercase.
hinglish_roman: Binomial system mein scientific naam ke do hisse hote hain — pehle genus naam capital letter se, phir species naam lowercase mein likhte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The scientific name Panthera tigris is written in italics when printed, with Panthera being the genus and tigris the species.
hinglish_roman: Panthera tigris ka scientific naam print mein italics mein likha jaata hai, jisme Panthera genus hai aur tigris species.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: A genus groups closely related species; for example, Panthera tigris (tiger) and Panthera leo (lion) are both in the genus Panthera.
hinglish_roman: Ek genus closely related species ko group karta hai; jaise Panthera tigris yaani tiger aur Panthera leo yaani lion dono Panthera genus mein hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Carl Woese proposed the three domain system in 1977, dividing life into Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya based on genetic data.
hinglish_roman: Carl Woese ne 1977 mein teen domain system propose kiya jisme genetic data ke aadhar par life ko Bacteria, Archaea aur Eukarya mein divide kiya gaya.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fossils are preserved remains of plants and animals found in layers of rocks, sand and mud, providing evidence of how life has changed over millions of years.
hinglish_roman: Fossils pedh-paudhon aur jaanwaron ke preserved remains hote hain jo rocks, ret aur mitti ki perton mein milte hain, aur yeh laakhon saalon mein jeevan kaise badla iski evidence dete hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Human activities like pollution, deforestation, overuse of resources and climate change are reducing biodiversity.
hinglish_roman: Pradushan, deforestation, resources ka zyaada use aur climate change jaise human activities biodiversity ko kam kar rahi hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: When one species disappears, others that depend on it may also decline, highlighting the interconnected nature of ecosystems.
hinglish_roman: Jab ek species khatam ho jaati hai, to usse dependent doosri species bhi ghatti ja sakti hain, jo ecosystems ki interconnected nature ko highlight karta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Can you explain what biodiversity means and why it is important for us?
hinglish_roman: Kya aap explain kar sakte hain biodiversity ka matlab kya hai aur yeh hamare liye kyun important hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the definition of endemic species? Can you give me an example from India?
hinglish_roman: Endemic species ki definition kya hoti hai? Kya aap mujhe India se koi example de sakte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the difference between autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition?
hinglish_roman: Autotrophic aur heterotrophic nutrition mein kya difference hota hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Can you explain what binomial nomenclature is and why scientists use it?
hinglish_roman: Kya aap explain kar sakte hain binomial nomenclature kya hota hai aur scientists ise kyun use karte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the difference between bryophytes and pteridophytes?
hinglish_roman: Bryophytes aur pteridophytes mein kya antar hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Can you explain Whittaker's five kingdom classification with the criteria used?
hinglish_roman: Kya aap Whittaker ka five kingdom classification aur usme use kiye gaye criteria explain kar sakte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What are biodiversity hotspots? Why is the Western Ghats considered one?
hinglish_roman: Biodiversity hotspots kya hote hain? Western Ghats ko ek hotspot kyun maana jaata hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the main difference between invertebrates and vertebrates?
hinglish_roman: Invertebrates aur vertebrates mein main difference kya hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Can you explain what a notochord is and what role it plays in animal classification?
hinglish_roman: Kya aap explain kar sakte hain notochord kya hota hai aur animal classification mein iska kya role hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is Kingdom Monera? Which organisms are placed in it and why?
hinglish_roman: Kingdom Monera kya hai? Ismein kaun se organisms rakhe jaate hain aur kyun?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the difference between gymnosperms and angiosperms? Can you give examples of each?
hinglish_roman: Gymnosperms aur angiosperms mein kya antar hai? Kya aap dono ke examples de sakte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: How does hierarchical classification work? What does each level represent?
hinglish_roman: Hierarchical classification kaise kaam karta hai? Har level kya represent karta hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Why are fungi classified in a separate kingdom even though they look like plants?
hinglish_roman: Fungi ko ek alag kingdom mein kyun classify kiya jaata hai jabki woh plants ki tarah dikhte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the definition of a species in biological classification?
hinglish_roman: Biological classification mein species ki definition kya hoti hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells? Can you give examples of organisms in each?
hinglish_roman: Prokaryotic aur eukaryotic cells mein kya antar hai? Kya dono ke organisms ke examples de sakte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Biodiversity is essential for every living organism on Earth.
hinglish_roman: Biodiversity har ek living organism ke liye Earth par jaruri hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
hinglish_with_error: Biodiversity har ek living organism ke liye Earth pe jaruri hota hai.
gec_explanation: 'Biodiversity' is singular and feminine in context; 'hota' (masculine agreement) should be 'hoti' or simply 'hai' for gender-neutral agreement.

original_english: Fungi are classified in a separate kingdom because they obtain nutrients by absorption from dead matter.
hinglish_roman: Fungi ko alag kingdom mein classify kiya gaya hai kyunki woh dead matter se absorption ke zariye nutrients prapt karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
hinglish_with_error: Fungi ko alag kingdom mein classify kiya gaya hai kyunki woh dead matter se absorb karke nutrients prapt karta hain.
gec_explanation: 'Fungi' is plural in usage here; the verb should be 'karte hain' not 'karta hain'.

original_english: Pteridophytes have vascular tissues — xylem and phloem — for transporting water and food throughout the plant.
hinglish_roman: Pteridophytes mein vascular tissues hote hain — xylem aur phloem — jo poore plant mein paani aur food transport karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
hinglish_with_error: Pteridophytes mein vascular tissue hote hain — xylem aur phloem — jo poore plant mein paani aur food transport karta hain.
gec_explanation: The subject 'xylem aur phloem' is plural; the correct verb form is 'karte hain', not 'karta hain'.

original_english: Binomial nomenclature was introduced by Carolus Linnaeus so that scientists worldwide could use a common naming system.
hinglish_roman: Binomial nomenclature Carolus Linnaeus ne isliye introduce kiya taaki duniyabhar ke scientists ek common naming system use kar sakein.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
hinglish_with_error: Binomial nomenclature Carolus Linnaeus ne isliye introduce kiya tha taaki duniyabhar ke scientists ek common naming system use kar saka.
gec_explanation: After 'taaki' (so that), the subjunctive form 'sakein' (plural) is correct, not 'saka' (singular past masculine).

original_english: When one species becomes extinct, the other species that depend on it may also be affected.
hinglish_roman: Jab ek species extinct ho jaati hai, to usse dependent doosri species bhi prabhavit ho sakti hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
hinglish_with_error: Jab ek species extinct ho jaata hai, to usse dependent doosri species bhi prabhavit ho sakti hain.
gec_explanation: 'Species' is treated as feminine in Hindi; 'ho jaata' (masculine) should be 'ho jaati' (feminine).

original_english: Biodiversity refers to the enormous variety of life forms found on Earth.
hinglish_roman: Biodiversity matlab hai Earth par paaye jaane wale living organisms ki enormous variety.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Endemic species are found naturally only in specific regions of the world and nowhere else.
hinglish_roman: Endemic species woh hoti hain jo sirf specific regions mein naturally payi jaati hain aur kahin aur nahi.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Biodiversity hotspots are regions with many endemic species that have also suffered significant habitat loss.
hinglish_roman: Biodiversity hotspots woh regions hain jahan endemic species ki badi sankhya hai aur significant habitat loss bhi hua hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Biological classification groups organisms based on shared characteristics and evolutionary relationships.
hinglish_roman: Biological classification mein organisms ko unki shared characteristics aur evolutionary relationships ke basis par group kiya jaata hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Aristotle, in the 4th century BCE, grouped animals based on their habitat — land, water and air.
hinglish_roman: Aristotle ne 4th century BCE mein animals ko unke habitat ke basis par — land, water aur air — group kiya tha.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The five kingdom classification includes Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.
hinglish_roman: Five kingdom classification mein Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae aur Animalia — yeh paanch kingdoms hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Bacteria and cyanobacteria are single-celled prokaryotes grouped under Kingdom Monera.
hinglish_roman: Bacteria aur cyanobacteria single-celled prokaryotes hain jo Kingdom Monera mein aate hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Protista includes single-celled eukaryotes like Amoeba, Paramecium and Euglena.
hinglish_roman: Protista mein single-celled eukaryotes aate hain jaise Amoeba, Paramecium aur Euglena.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fungi have cell walls made of chitin and obtain nutrients by absorbing them from dead or decaying matter.
hinglish_roman: Fungi ki cell wall chitin se bani hoti hai aur yeh dead ya decaying matter se nutrients absorb karke obtain karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Plants are multicellular, autotrophic organisms whose cells have a rigid cell wall made primarily of cellulose.
hinglish_roman: Plants multicellular aur autotrophic organisms hain jinke cells ki rigid cell wall mainly cellulose se bani hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Thallophytes form a simple thallus body and are mostly found in water or moist environments.
hinglish_roman: Thallophytes ka body ek simple thallus hota hai aur yeh zyaadatar water ya moist environments mein milte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom because they need water for reproduction.
hinglish_roman: Bryophytes ko plant kingdom ke amphibians kaha jaata hai kyunki inhe reproduction ke liye water chahiye hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Pteridophytes like ferns have true roots, stems and leaves with vascular tissues for water and food transport.
hinglish_roman: Pteridophytes jaise ferns mein true roots, stems aur leaves hote hain aur inme water aur food transport ke liye vascular tissues bhi hote hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Gymnosperms produce seeds that are not enclosed in fruits, and are often exposed on cones.
hinglish_roman: Gymnosperms aise seeds produce karte hain jo fruits mein enclosed nahi hote aur aksar cones par exposed rehte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Angiosperms are flowering plants with the most complex body organisation among all plant groups.
hinglish_roman: Angiosperms flowering plants hain aur inke paas sabse complex body organisation hoti hai sab plant groups mein.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Animals are multicellular, heterotrophic organisms that depend on other organisms for food.
hinglish_roman: Animals multicellular aur heterotrophic organisms hain jo apne food ke liye doosre organisms par depend karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Invertebrates lack a notochord and include phyla such as Porifera, Cnidaria, Nematoda and Arthropoda.
hinglish_roman: Invertebrates mein notochord nahi hoti aur inme Porifera, Cnidaria, Nematoda aur Arthropoda jaise phyla aate hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Sponges belong to Porifera and are multicellular but lack true tissues and organs.
hinglish_roman: Sponges Porifera mein aate hain — yeh multicellular hote hain lekin inme true tissues aur organs nahi hote.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Arthropods have jointed appendages and a hard exoskeleton that reduces water loss and provides protection.
hinglish_roman: Arthropods mein jointed appendages aur hard exoskeleton hoti hai jo water loss kam karti hai aur protection bhi deti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Vertebrates possess a vertebral column (backbone) that supports the body and protects the spinal cord.
hinglish_roman: Vertebrates mein vertebral column yaani backbone hoti hai jo body ko support karti hai aur spinal cord ko protect karti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Vertebrates are classified into five groups: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
hinglish_roman: Vertebrates ko paanch groups mein classify kiya jaata hai — fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds aur mammals.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Classification follows a hierarchy from Kingdom down to Species, with each lower level sharing more common features.
hinglish_roman: Classification Kingdom se Species tak ek hierarchy follow karti hai jisme lower level par organisms mein zyaada common features hote hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Binomial nomenclature was introduced by Carolus Linnaeus in the 18th century to give organisms a universal scientific name.
hinglish_roman: Binomial nomenclature 18th century mein Carolus Linnaeus ne introduce kiya tha taaki organisms ko ek universal scientific name diya ja sake.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: In binomial nomenclature, the genus name starts with a capital letter and the species name is in lowercase.
hinglish_roman: Binomial nomenclature mein genus name capital letter se start hota hai aur species name lowercase mein likhte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The three domain system proposed by Carl Woese classifies life into Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya based on DNA.
hinglish_roman: Carl Woese ka three domain system DNA ke basis par life ko Bacteria, Archaea aur Eukarya mein classify karta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fungi play an important ecological role as decomposers by breaking down dead organic matter.
hinglish_roman: Fungi ek important ecological role play karte hain — yeh dead organic matter ko break down karke decomposers ki tarah kaam karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Mangrove forests with rich biodiversity act as physical barriers that reduce the impact of cyclones.
hinglish_roman: Rich biodiversity wale mangrove forests physical barriers ki tarah kaam karte hain aur cyclones ke impact ko reduce karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The Nilgiri tahr and the Lion-tailed macaque are endemic species found only in India.
hinglish_roman: Nilgiri tahr aur Lion-tailed macaque endemic species hain jo sirf India mein payi jaati hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The scientific name of a tiger is Panthera tigris, where Panthera is the genus and tigris is the species.
hinglish_roman: Tiger ka scientific name Panthera tigris hai, jisme Panthera genus hai aur tigris species ka naam hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Mushroom cultivation is an accessible livelihood option requiring minimal space and low investment.
hinglish_roman: Mushroom cultivation ek accessible livelihood option hai jisme bahut kam space aur low investment chahiye hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Molluscs like snails and squids have soft bodies and show organ system level organisation.
hinglish_roman: Snails aur squids jaise Molluscs ke soft bodies hote hain aur inme organ system level organisation hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Parasitic flatworms use hooks and suckers to attach firmly to host tissues.
hinglish_roman: Parasitic flatworms hooks aur suckers use karke host tissues se firmly attach rehte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Cnidarians like Hydra and jellyfish have tissue-level organisation and use tentacles to capture prey.
hinglish_roman: Hydra aur jellyfish jaise Cnidarians mein tissue-level organisation hoti hai aur yeh prey pakadne ke liye tentacles use karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Spirogyra is an example of a Thallophyte (alga) found in water or moist environments.
hinglish_roman: Spirogyra ek Thallophyte yaani alga ka example hai jo water ya moist environments mein milta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: A genus groups closely related species that share common features, for example Panthera includes tigers and lions.
hinglish_roman: Genus mein closely related species hoti hain jinke common features share hote hain — jaise Panthera genus mein tigers aur lions dono aate hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Biodiversity is essential for us — every organism plays a role in keeping nature stable and functioning.
hinglish_roman: Biodiversity hamare liye bahut zaroori hai. Har organism nature ko stable aur functioning rakhne mein koi na koi role play karta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: The Western Ghats and the Himalayas are biodiversity hotspots in India.
hinglish_roman: Western Ghats aur Himalayas India ke biodiversity hotspots hain. Yahan endemic species ki sankhya bahut zyaada hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: In the two kingdom system all organisms were divided into Plantae and Animalia. But this created confusion for unicellular organisms like Amoeba.
hinglish_roman: Two kingdom system mein sabhi organisms ko Plantae aur Animalia mein divide kiya gaya tha. Lekin Amoeba jaise unicellular organisms ko kahan rakhein, isko lekar confusion thi.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Cyanobacteria were among the first organisms to produce oxygen through photosynthesis.
hinglish_roman: Cyanobacteria pehle organisms mein se thay jo photosynthesis ke through oxygen produce karte the. Unki wajah se aaj Earth ka atmosphere oxygen se bhara hua hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fungi reproduce by forming spores and grow best in warm and moist conditions.
hinglish_roman: Fungi spores banake reproduce karte hain. Yeh warm aur moist conditions mein sabse achhe se grow karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Gymnosperms do not need water for fertilisation. Their seeds are exposed on cones, not enclosed in fruits.
hinglish_roman: Gymnosperms ko fertilisation ke liye water ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Inke seeds cones par exposed rehte hain, fruits ke andar nahi.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Echinoderms like starfish have a hard internal skeleton made of calcium carbonate.
hinglish_roman: Echinoderms jaise starfish mein calcium carbonate se bana ek hard internal skeleton hota hai. Yeh unhe protection aur controlled movement deta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Lichens are bioindicators for air quality — they change colour in the presence of air pollutants.
hinglish_roman: Lichens air quality ke bioindicators hain. Yeh air pollutants ke presence mein apna colour change kar lete hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Hierarchical classification works like an address — it helps scientists locate and identify an organism precisely.
hinglish_roman: Hierarchical classification ek address ki tarah kaam karti hai. Isse scientists kisi bhi organism ko precisely identify aur locate kar sakte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Hortus Malabaricus was compiled in the 17th century showing how traditional knowledge and science can work together.
hinglish_roman: Hortus Malabaricus 17th century mein compile kiya gaya tha. Yeh dikhata hai ki traditional knowledge aur science ek saath kaise kaam kar sakte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Protochordates like Amphioxus possess a notochord at least once during their life cycle.
hinglish_roman: Amphioxus jaise protochordates mein apne life cycle mein kam se kam ek baar notochord hoti hai. Yeh simple forms se notochord wale animals ke evolution ko samajhne mein help karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Birbal Sahni was a pioneering Indian scientist who contributed to palaeobotany.
hinglish_roman: Birbal Sahni ek pioneering Indian scientist the. Unhone palaeobotany mein bahut important contributions diye.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Ram Bux Singh is known as the Father of Modern Biogas in India.
hinglish_roman: Ram Bux Singh ko India mein Father of Modern Biogas kaha jaata hai. Unhone 1957 mein India ka pehla scientifically designed biogas plant establish kiya tha.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Flatworms show bilateral symmetry, which allows better coordination of directional movement.
hinglish_roman: Flatworms mein bilateral symmetry hoti hai. Isse unhe directional movement mein better coordination milta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Angiosperms produce flowers that attract pollinators and fruits that help disperse seeds.
hinglish_roman: Angiosperms flowers produce karte hain jo pollinators ko attract karte hain. Aur inke fruits seeds ko nayi jagah disperse karne mein help karte hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Annelids like earthworms have segmented bodies which allow greater flexibility and precise movement.
hinglish_roman: Earthworms jaise Annelids ka body segmented hota hai. Yeh segmentation unhe greater flexibility aur precise movement deta hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Pakke Tiger Reserve in Arunachal Pradesh supports four species of hornbills, each in different forest zones.
hinglish_roman: Pakke Tiger Reserve Arunachal Pradesh mein hai. Yahan hornbills ki char species milti hain aur har ek alag forest zone mein rehti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Fossils of ancient cyanobacteria called stromatolites were found in Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.
hinglish_roman: Rajasthan aur Madhya Pradesh mein ancient cyanobacteria ke fossils mile hain jine stromatolites kaha jaata hai. Yeh Earth par life ke kuch sabse purane evidences hain.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Classification helps identify organisms that are under threat of extinction, supporting biodiversity conservation.
hinglish_roman: Classification se hum extinction ke khatra mein aaye organisms ko identify kar sakte hain. Isse biodiversity conservation mein bahut help milti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Yeast is unicellular but classified under Fungi because its cell wall is made of chitin.
hinglish_roman: Yeast unicellular hai lekin ise Fungi mein classify kiya jaata hai. Kyunki iski cell wall chitin se bani hoti hai.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is biodiversity and why is it important?
hinglish_roman: Biodiversity kya hai aur yeh kyun zaroori hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Why do scientists classify living organisms?
hinglish_roman: Scientists living organisms ko classify kyun karte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the difference between Monera and Protista?
hinglish_roman: Monera aur Protista mein kya difference hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is binomial nomenclature and what are its rules?
hinglish_roman: Binomial nomenclature kya hota hai aur iske kya rules hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What makes Bryophytes different from Thallophytes?
hinglish_roman: Bryophytes aur Thallophytes mein kya fark hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Why are Pteridophytes more advanced than Bryophytes?
hinglish_roman: Pteridophytes Bryophytes se zyada advanced kyun hote hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the difference between vertebrates and invertebrates?
hinglish_roman: Vertebrates aur invertebrates mein kya difference hota hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Why are Fungi placed in a separate kingdom from plants?
hinglish_roman: Fungi ko plants se alag, ek separate kingdom mein kyun rakha jaata hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is an endemic species? Give an example from India.
hinglish_roman: Endemic species kya hoti hai? India se ek example do.
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: How does the three domain system differ from the five kingdom classification?
hinglish_roman: Three domain system aur five kingdom classification mein kya fark hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the role of classification in identifying species under threat of extinction?
hinglish_roman: Extinction ke khatra mein aaye species ko identify karne mein classification ka kya role hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Why do classification systems keep changing over time?
hinglish_roman: Classification systems time ke saath kyun change hote rehte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What features are used to classify living organisms into the five kingdoms?
hinglish_roman: Five kingdoms mein organisms ko classify karne ke liye kaunse features use kiye jaate hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Why are Gymnosperms better suited to cold and dry regions than Angiosperms?
hinglish_roman: Gymnosperms cold aur dry regions mein Angiosperms se zyada suited kyun hote hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the significance of vascular tissues in Pteridophytes?
hinglish_roman: Pteridophytes mein vascular tissues ki kya significance hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: How does the exoskeleton of Arthropods help them survive in dry environments?
hinglish_roman: Arthropods ki exoskeleton unhe dry environments mein survive karne mein kaise help karti hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the role of fungi as decomposers in an ecosystem?
hinglish_roman: Ecosystem mein fungi decomposers ki tarah kya role play karte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: What is the basis of the hierarchical classification system?
hinglish_roman: Hierarchical classification system ka kya basis hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: How do biodiversity hotspots help in conservation of endemic species?
hinglish_roman: Biodiversity hotspots endemic species ki conservation mein kaise help karte hain?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

original_english: Why is Amoeba classified under Protista and not under Animalia even though it moves?
hinglish_roman: Amoeba move karta hai phir bhi ise Animalia mein nahi balki Protista mein classify kyun kiya jaata hai?
chapter: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification
